item.title: Tankers attacked as Trump mulls new strikes in "little war" with Iran
item.description: Two oil tankers were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz as President Trump threatened further strikes on Iran, while downplaying the "relatively little" 6-month war.

item.title: Whistleblower warns Postal Service's mail ballot portal is "rushed," "untested"
item.description: The whistleblower, described by lawyers as a federal official, disclosed information about the Postal Service's new mail-voting procedures to Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut.

item.title: Tropical Storm Edouard strengthens as it nears Louisiana, Texas coasts
item.description: Tropical Storm Edouard could hit parts of the Texas and Louisiana Gulf Coasts with near-hurricane conditions today, the National Hurricane Center warns.

item.title: American among thousands missing in Nepal contacted, officials say
item.description: Nepali officials tell CBS News they have contacted a U.S. national among the more than 4,000 people still missing in the wake of the deadly flash floods.

item.title: Face Your Finances and Finance Your Face | Money Moves with Jill Schlesinger
item.description: Should Botox be a line item on your budget? Special guest host and certified financial planner Kayla Sabbagh joins Jill and Mark to discuss the rise in cosmetic procedures among young people — and how to manage your face and your finances. Plus, can you guess the price of private school in Indiana? Jill, Mark, and Kayla counsel caller Rachel on whether or not she can afford to pay to send her kid to private preschool.

item.title: Mass. primary features Markey vs. Moulton and more key races
item.description: Massachusetts is holding its 2026 primary election on Tuesday, with the ballot featuring a Senate race between Ed Markey and Seth Moulton.

item.title: The market forces quietly adding thousands to patient bills
item.description: The true cost of "vertical integration": Patients directed to a higher-priced location for procedures. Or forced to buy from their insurer's wholly owned pharmacy, which may not stock the drug prescribed or provide it at the lowest price.

item.title: Woman attacked by otter while swimming in Lake Tahoe, receives nearly 40 stitches
item.description: An open-water swimmer says a routine morning swim in Lake Tahoe turned into a frightening encounter when an otter attacked her underwater.

item.title: Families of those missing after Nepal floods struggle to cling to hope as death toll passes 1,000
item.description: As the death toll from the Nepal floods passes 1000, Americans with loved ones among the nearly 4,000 people missing are still hoping for miracles.

item.title: A look at search, rescue and recovery efforts in Nepal
item.description: On Monday, search, rescue and recovery efforts continued in Nepal after the devastating floods last week. Around 4,200 people are still missing and at least 903 people have been killed, according to Nepal's national disaster agency. Videos show some of the efforts.

item.title: U.S.-Venezuela oil deal will rely on North American Blue Energy Partners
item.description: The Trump administration's plan to take a stake in tens of billions of barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves will hinge on a private company called North American Blue Energy Partners, the White House announced Monday.

item.title: 3 friends went hiking in the Grand Canyon. 1 died, 2 were reported missing.
item.description: At least two people were killed after flash floods swept through parts of Grand Canyon National Park over the weekend.

item.title: St. Louis becomes the latest battleground in fight over data centers
item.description: "We have to be very careful about where and how we install these large data centers," said Kasey Fowler-Finn, a biologist at St. Louis University, who is among a group suing to halt a data center development.

item.title: 2 dead, at least 1 missing after Grand Canyon hit by flash floods
item.description: Violent flash floods hit the Grand Canyon's Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch area, causing "extensive damage" to the park's water infrastructure.

item.title: Supreme Court continues to allow construction of Trump's White House ballroom
item.description: The Supreme Court divided 5-4 in allowing construction of the new White House ballroom to continue.

item.title: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigning after friction with Hegseth
item.description: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is resigning, the White House confirmed.

item.title: Could an American win men's singles at this year's U.S. Open?
item.description: The Athletic's Lukas Weese joins CBS News to discuss who has the best chances with the U.S. Open tennis tournament underway in New York City.

item.title: What to know after John Galliano's Met Gala exhibit canceled
item.description: John Galliano's exhibit for the 2027 Met Gala has been canceled after weeks of backlash over his past antisemitic and racist comments. CBS News fashion contributor Lauren Sherman reports.

item.title: Guilty verdict in 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur
item.description: Duane "Keffe D" Davis, 63, was charged with murder with a deadly weapon with the intent to promote, further or assist a criminal gang in Shakur's death.

item.title: Jury finds Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty in 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur
item.description: A Las Vegas jury on Monday found Duane "Keffe D" Davis guilty in the 1996 murder of Tupac Shakur. CBS News legal reporter Katrina Kaufman has more.

item.title: Parents, coaches fighting at youth games leads to cancellations and bans
item.description: Two youth football coaches near Pittsburgh had a fight on the field over the weekend, earning suspensions from the league and adding to a growing list of adults behaving badly at their kids' sporting events. Mark Strassmann reports.

item.title: U.S. launches its first strike on Iran in over a month, regime retaliates
item.description: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation to President Trump on Monday. Over the weekend, the war with Iran entered its seventh month, with the first exchange of attacks in weeks. Weijia Jiang reports from the White House.

item.title: Police shoot woman who allegedly stabbed 2 people in Times Square
item.description: Warning: Disturbing footage. NYPD officers opened fire on a woman allegedly wielding at least one knife in Times Square on Monday. Tom Hanson reports from New York City.

item.title: 8/31: CBS Evening News
item.description: A deadly flood disaster hit the Grand Canyon; a tropical storm warning was issued for the coasts of Texas and Louisiana.

item.title: FTC and 22 states sue Amazon over alleged secret ad surcharge scheme
item.description: Regulators allege that sellers and brands were overcharged by tens of billions of dollars through secretly inflated ad prices.

item.title: Kalshi bans ex-congressman George Santos for life after suspicious trades
item.description: George Santos faces a lifetime ban from Kalshi after failing to cooperate with the prediction market's investigation into his alleged unlawful trades.

item.title: Will Trump's Venezuela oil deal ease U.S. gas prices?
item.description: The deal involves developing 17 strategic oil fields in Venezuela, an undertaking that experts said could take years.

item.title: D4vd pleads not guilty in Celeste Rivas Hernandez murder case
item.description: The 21-year-old singer is accused of killing the 14-year-old Inland Empire girl after a lengthy sexual relationship.

item.title: John Galliano's Met Gala exhibit canceled amid backlash
item.description: The Met's decision to highlight the work by designer John Galliano sparked widespread controversy due to his history of antisemitic and racist comments.

item.title: Trump says U.S. now has control of over 60 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves
item.description: President Trump announced a deal to grant the U.S. control of more than 60 billion barrels of proven Venezuelan oil reserves.
